issues.legal_issue: A civil appeal cannot proceed without a necessary party who was included in the appeal below when the appellants knew of that party’s participation and sought to add the party only belatedly without due diligence.
material_facts: After the original plaintiff died during the appeal in the High Court, the plaintiff’s legal representatives, including another son, were brought on record, and that son was represented by counsel.
The appellants knew that the son had been made a party but did not include him in their appeal to the Supreme Court.
The appellants offered no good reason for omitting him and sought to add him only after the appeal came before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The late application to add the omitted party was refused, and the appeal was dismissed as not properly instituted.
issues.legal_principle: A necessary party must be joined in an appeal. An appellant who knew of the party’s participation below cannot rely on an unclear judgment to excuse the omission, and a belated request to add the party may be refused where the appellant did not act with due diligence. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_appeal and omitted_person_was_party_in_appeal_below and omitted_person_was_necessary_party and appellants_knew_of_participation and late_joinder_request_lacked_due_diligence

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal.
predicates.omitted_person_was_party_in_appeal_below: The person omitted from the current appeal had been made a party to the appeal below.
predicates.omitted_person_was_necessary_party: The court treated the omitted person as necessary to the appeal.
predicates.appellants_knew_of_participation: The appellants knew that the person had participated as a party in the appeal below.
predicates.late_joinder_request_lacked_due_diligenc: The appellants sought to add the person only belatedly and had not acted with due diligence.

issues.definition: When a civil appellant knowingly omits a necessary person who was a party below and seeks joinder only belatedly without due diligence, the appeal is dismissed for nonjoinder.

issues.legal_issue: A civil appeal cannot proceed without a person who was added as a party in an earlier appeal when the appellants knew of that joinder, omitted the person from later appeals, and sought joinder only belatedly.
material_facts: After a party to the suit died during the first appeal, some of that party’s legal representatives applied to continue the appeal.

The opposing party objected that the deceased party’s estate would not be fully represented unless another legal representative was joined; the first appellate court accepted an application to join that person as a respondent.
The appeal was dismissed, and the appellants omitted the joined person from both their second appeal and their appeal to the Supreme Court, although they knew of the earlier joinder.
The appellants sought to add the person only after the appeal reached the Supreme Court. They also contended that the person had no interest in the premises.
issues.conclusion: The late application to add the omitted party was refused, the contention about that person’s interest was not considered in the person’s absence, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A party who was joined in an earlier appeal cannot be omitted from a later appeal to the advantage of appellants who knew of that joinder. A belated request to add the person may be refused where the appellants were not duly diligent, and a claim that the absent person has no interest cannot be decided in that person’s absence. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_appeal and person_was_joined_in_earlier_appeal and person_was_omitted_from_later_appeals and appellants_knew_of_earlier_joinder and late_joinder_request_lacked_due_diligence

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal.
predicates.person_was_joined_in_earlier_appeal: The person had been made a party in an earlier appeal concerning the dispute.
predicates.person_was_omitted_from_later_appeals: The appellants did not include the person in later appeals concerning the dispute.
predicates.appellants_knew_of_earlier_joinder: The appellants knew that the person had been made a party in the earlier appeal.
predicates.late_joinder_request_lacked_due_diligenc: The appellants sought to add the person only belatedly and had not acted with due diligence.

issues.definition: When civil appellants knowingly omit from later appeals a person joined in an earlier appeal and seek joinder only belatedly without due diligence, the appeal is dismissed for nonjoinder.
